body.text: In this episode of The Kashmir Notebook, Gowhar Geelani speaks with theatre maker and filmmaker Arshad Mushtaq about Kashmir’s long tradition of storytelling, theatre, and the role of the Kashmiri language in preserving cultural memory. Mushtaq discusses his journey as a theatre maker, filmmaker and storyteller, and the making of his film “Aks-e-Ghalib Dast-e-Shifa”, which brings Mirza Ghalib’s poetry to Kashmiri audiences.

The conversation also looks at Bhand Pather, Kashmir’s traditional folk theatre, its roots in social and political commentary, and how state patronage and changing cultural practices have affected the form. Mushtaq speaks about taking Kashmiri theatre and local stories to global audiences while retaining their indigenous idiom, the importance of memory and cultural identity, artistic independence, and the need to create space for local artists and filmmakers. He also discusses the future of theatre, the role of young artists, the impact of AI on creative work, and why Kashmiri storytellers have a responsibility to take their stories to the world.
